comments.body:
## Tenth instance, found after this epic was filed — and it sharpens the diagnosis

Bug a371-fb42-32c5-48bd (found by the c5b3 agent, 2026-08-05): two test modules carry a broken
`tests.`-rooted import —

    tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py:21
    tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py:21
        from tests.unit import _audit_page_helpers as H

`tests` is not an importable package under CI's bare `pytest` invocation, so these imports are
BROKEN. They do not fail today only because both files call `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")` on
the line above, and the `[ui]` extra is absent from the lean CI suite — so collection skips
before the broken import is reached.

## Why this belongs in this epic rather than as an unrelated import bug

It is the family's purest form so far. The tests are not merely vacuous, they are vacuous
CONDITIONALLY, and the condition is inverted from what anyone would assume: they read as covered
everywhere, and they break precisely where the optional extra IS installed — i.e. exactly the
environment where their coverage was supposed to matter. A skip is masking a defect rather than
representing an absent capability.

This is a distinct sub-kind from the ones in the original diagnosis, and worth adding to it:

  **F. Skip-masked breakage** — a test that cannot run for an unrelated reason (missing optional
  dependency, capability probe, platform guard) and whose skip conceals that it could not run
  even if the dependency were present. The skip is read as "not applicable here", when the truth
  is "would fail anywhere".

Note this sub-kind is MECHANICALLY DETECTABLE and therefore lands in the recommendation's part 1
(CI structural meta-gate), not part 2: a checker can import-resolve every skipped module and
assert the skip is the ONLY thing preventing execution. That is a narrow, decidable question.

Also worth recording as evidence for part 3 of the recommendation (mutation proof as the
expectation): this was found only because an agent ran the repo-wide sweep after fixing its own
instance of a `tests.`-rooted import. Nothing in the lifecycle asked for that sweep. It has now
happened twice in one session — 34c2's sweep found 8a5e's four guards, and 7e90's found 1909's
eleven steps. Three sweeps, three multi-instance discoveries, zero of them prompted by a gate.

comments.body:
## EMPIRICAL VALIDATION of recommendation part 1 — the anti-vacuity assertion caught a new vacuous guard AS IT WAS BEING WRITTEN

Recording this because it is the strongest evidence in this epic, and it was produced by accident
rather than by looking for it.

Bug 9baf-06ce-60ba-4f0b (two CloudWatch alarms with no `alarm_actions`) was dispatched with a
requirement drawn from this epic's recommendation: add a guard, AND give the guard an
anti-vacuity assertion that its scanned population is non-empty.

What happened, in the agent's own account:

> The anti-vacuity assertion earned its place within a minute of existing. My first parser
> matched the resource header against the *masked* text, where quoted strings are blanked, so it
> found **zero** blocks — and `test_every_alarm_declares_alarm_actions` **passed vacuously**
> while the `>= 13` assertion failed loudly and exposed the bug.

So a BRAND NEW guard, written by an agent that had been explicitly warned about vacuity, in a
session whose entire theme was vacuous checks, was itself vacuous on first attempt. The only
reason it did not ship that way is the population assertion.

## Why this matters for the recommendation

It answers the strongest objection to part 1 — that an anti-vacuity convention is bureaucratic
overhead for a rare failure. The measured rate here is not rare. Across this session:

- 5 pre-existing guards found vacuous (34c2 plus 8a5e's four)
- 11 CI gate steps unguarded (1909)
- 1 test double more permissive than the real tool (c5b3)
- 2 tests skip-masked into permanent non-execution (a371)
- **1 new guard vacuous on first write, caught by the assertion (9baf)**

The last is qualitatively different from the others. The rest are archaeology — debt accumulated
before anyone was watching. This one is a NEW defect, introduced by an informed author, and
prevented. That is the difference between the closed prior-art tickets (6924, 4168, 003d — all
remedial sweeps) and a mechanism.

It also cost essentially nothing: one assertion, written at the same time as the guard, by the
same author, in the same file.

## Refinement to part 1 this suggests

The 9baf guard's failure mode is worth generalizing: the parser found zero blocks because it
searched TEXT THAT HAD BEEN DELIBERATELY BLANKED (comment/string masking). That is a plausible
mistake for any scanning check, not a one-off. So the convention should be stated as a property
of the POPULATION, not of the parse:

    assert the scanned population is non-empty AND matches an independently-known count

9baf used `>= 13` — a number the author knew from outside the parser. A bare `len(x) > 0` would
also have caught this instance, but an independently-sourced expected count is strictly stronger
and no harder to write.

## Also worth noting for part 3 (mutation proof as expectation)

The same agent mutation-checked both directions: re-deleting the alarm's `alarm_actions` returned
the guard to RED, and pointing the parser at an empty directory failed the COUNT assertion rather
than passing. The second half of that is the anti-vacuity property tested as a first-class
behavior, not assumed.

comments.body:
## Relationship to epic 3147 — adjacent and complementary, NOT duplicate

Operator asked whether this epic is already covered by an in-progress epic on tightening AC
requirements. Checked all four candidates. Answer: no, but 3147 is close enough to be worth
linking.

    3147-7b57-5263-4e5d  in_progress  Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence:
                                      force measurement provenance into the record
    8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864  in_progress  T15 overlay-derisk: prove risky mechanisms out-of-loop
    facb-44c3-2ada-41ee  open         Ratchet approved maintainability/reliability gates
    55de-25ab-ca20-4c79  open         Review-gate project configuration tool + UX

8fc2, facb and 55de are clearly different work — pre-validating risky mechanisms, enabling
existing lint/mypy ratchets, and gate config UX respectively.

## 3147 vs this epic — different LAYERS of the same concern

- **3147 targets the EVIDENCE an author supplies.** ADR 0061 (now merged) requires attested
  evidence to declare its measurement provenance: you claimed it works — how did you MEASURE it?
  Its instrument is a plan-review criterion `project.measurement-provenance` triggering on
  `[operator-attested]`.
- **This epic targets the CHECK MECHANISM.** Not "is the author's claim grounded" but "can the
  guard that validates claims actually FAIL for the reason it exists".

Their own framings are complementary in a way worth preserving. 3147's context states **"The
gates performed to their design envelope"** — the gates worked as designed, but the design did not
demand grounded evidence. This epic's finding is the mirror image: several gates did NOT work as
designed, because they scanned an empty population.

    3147:  the gates are asking the wrong question
    6117:  some gates are not asking anything at all

## Recommendation: keep separate, linked

Three reasons not to fold this into 3147:
1. The interventions differ. 3147's is a plan-review criterion over ticket text; this epic's
   primary recommendation is a CI structural meta-gate over scanning checks, plus a code-review
   criterion. Different code, different stage, different failure signal.
2. 3147 is nearly complete — its ONLY child (f161, "Force measurement provenance into attested
   evidence") is closed, and its Gerrit change 1423 merged today. Folding a large new scope into
   an epic at that stage reopens something ready to finish.
3. This epic is still awaiting approval and may be adopted in part. Attaching it to an in-flight
   epic would couple that decision to 3147's completion.

## Worth checking separately

3147 is `in_progress` with its only child closed and that child's change now merged. It may be
closeable. Flagged rather than acted on, since it belongs to another work stream.

compiled_state.description:
# RECOMMENDATION AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL — do not decompose or implement yet

Filed 2026-08-05 at the operator's request after a single session surfaced nine instances of one
defect family. The analysis and recommendation are below; the operator decides whether to adopt,
which stage to put it in, and whether to fund it.

## The family

Nine defects found in one session, all the same shape: **a check that cannot fail for the reason
it exists**. Not absent checks — present, passing, and load-bearing in someone's reasoning.

| ticket | instance |
|---|---|
| 34c2 | AST guard pinned to ONE file; a module split moved the policed construct away, and it passed unconditionally |
| 8a5e | four MORE of the same, found only by sweeping after 34c2. One was doubly vacuous: its literal line-prefixes could not match the absolute import spelling the code actually uses |
| 2c58 | inert-config gate matches bare attribute names GLOBALLY, so a field whose name is reused anywhere escapes it |
| 7e90 | CI gate hard-failed on definition-vs-tree skew; the governing rule existed only as a code COMMENT, and was violated within hours of being written |
| 1909 | ELEVEN more unguarded steps, two of them breaking builds live |
| c5b3 | the fake `scc` test double emitted per-file data unconditionally while real scc requires `--by-file` — so the one test positioned to catch a fabricated-zero bug was structurally blind to it |
| dce2, a573 | config fields with zero read sites; the gate that should have caught a573 could not, per 2c58 |
| 5e53 | module-size hard cap with NO leading indicator: 40 files over 700 LOC, three within two lines of a hard CI failure, every instance discovered by an already-blocked contributor |
| 858c | close gate cannot express an N/A criterion, forcing a tick that falsely asserts completion |

## Prior art — this recurred

It has been addressed before, and the tickets are CLOSED:
`6924-0034` (epic, "Post-migration test & CI quality hardening"), `4168-c28e`
("Mutation testing: identify and prune change-detector tests"), `003d-e6b0`
("Replace hasattr/constant existence tests with behavioral provocation"),
`0f8f-ec8a` ("tests overlay: full behavioral-testing standard"),
`5ef2-6e74` ("Rewrite tautological conflict-resolver echo-suppression test"),
`d006-759b` (module-size report "toothless").

That prior work was REMEDIAL — find the bad checks, fix them. It did not leave a mechanism that
prevents new ones, which is why the family is back. A recommendation that is only another sweep
will produce the same outcome in three months.

## Diagnosis: two sub-kinds needing different mechanisms

**A. Mechanically detectable** — scope rot (34c2, 8a5e), global-name matching (2c58), unguarded
steps (7e90, 1909), inert config (dce2, a573), missing leading indicator (5e53). In every case a
program can decide the question, because the check declares a target population and the
population is empty, wrong, or unbounded.

**B. Judgment-dependent** — test-double fidelity (c5b3), N/A expressiveness (858c). No sweep
finds these; they need a reader who understands what the check is FOR. c5b3's stub was
syntactically fine and passing.

## Recommendation

**Do BOTH, at two different stages. Neither alone is sufficient.**

**1. A CI structural meta-gate for sub-kind A — the higher-leverage half.**

Adopt as a repo-wide convention: *every scanning/structural check must declare its target
population and assert that population is NON-EMPTY and covers what it claims.* Then enforce that
in CI the way `1909` already proved works — parse, enumerate, fail on any check lacking the
assertion.

This is not speculative. Three enforcement gates of exactly this shape already exist and work:
1909's workflow-step sweep (with a vacuity assertion on the detector itself), the module-size
contract, and the 6754 config-read gate. The recommendation is to generalize a proven local
pattern, not invent one.

Put it in **CI, not plan review** — plan review runs before code exists and cannot verify a
population; and **not completion verification**, which reads narrative evidence rather than code.

**2. A code-review criterion for sub-kind B.**

Something close to: *"Does this change add or modify a check — a test, guard, gate, or test
double? If so, does it demonstrate the check can FAIL for the reason it exists, and does any
double model the real thing's CONSTRAINTS rather than only its happy path?"*

Code review is the right stage because it sees the diff and can reason about intent. It should be
ADVISORY first, not blocking, until its false-positive rate is known.

**3. The cross-cutting change, and the cheapest one: make mutation proof the expectation for
check-modifying changes.**

Every genuinely trustworthy fix this session did this VOLUNTARILY — 8a5e, 7e90, 1909 and c5b3 all
mutation-checked in both directions, and in 8a5e's case the decisive evidence was that the
SUPERSEDED predicate stayed GREEN under the same mutation. That contrast is what distinguishes
"the guard is clean" from "the guard is vacuous", and nothing in the current lifecycle asks for
it. Making it expected rather than exceptional is the single highest-value item here and costs
almost nothing to state.

## What I would NOT do

- **Not another remediation sweep alone.** That is what the closed prior-art tickets did.
- **Not a blocking gate on day one.** A false-positive-prone blocking check on "is this check
  vacuous" would itself become something people route around.
- **Not plan review.** Wrong stage; it cannot see the code.
- **Not one ticket per instance.** That is the pattern that produced 5e53's forty-file backlog and
  three separate one-file emergencies in one session.

## Open questions for the operator

- Adopt one, two, or all three parts?
- Should the CI meta-gate be blocking from the start, or warn-only until its noise is measured?
- Is the anti-vacuity convention worth retrofitting to existing checks (a bounded sweep), or
  applied only to new and modified ones going forward?

## Not acceptance criteria yet

Deliberately none. This ticket is a recommendation for approval; ACs should be written after the
operator decides scope, since the shape differs substantially between the three parts.
compiled_state.title: Catch vacuous checks: a lifecycle step for checks that cannot fail for the reason they exist
